description: Shared contract for hashtag extraction from a note body (design doc §4.6, §7.3). Kotlin implements this in android/.../notes/TagParsing.kt; Notes.Shared implements the same rules in C# (T042). §7.3 names tag parsing as one of the places the two will drift, so both test suites execute THIS file rather than their own examples. If they disagree, a test fails instead of tags quietly differing between devices.
rules: A tag is '#' followed by one or more of: Unicode letter, Unicode digit, underscore, hyphen.
The run must contain at least one letter, so issue references like '#123' in prose are not tags.
The '#' must be preceded by start-of-input, a line start, or whitespace. This excludes 'example.com#anchor' and 'C#'.
Tags are lowercased, so '#Work' and '#work' are one tag. note_tags is keyed (noteId, tag) and would otherwise hold both.
Fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~, up to 3 leading spaces) are skipped entirely, so pasted '#include' and CSS '#fff' do not tag the note. An unclosed fence runs to end of input, per CommonMark.
Results are de-duplicated and returned in order of first appearance.
knownLimits: Indented (4-space) code blocks are NOT skipped — only fenced ones. Fences are what people actually paste.

Inline code spans are NOT parsed. '`#fff`' happens to be excluded anyway because a backtick is not whitespace, but 'see `#fff`' would tag. Accepted: full inline parsing means matching Markdig exactly, which is the divergence §7.3 warns about.
Parenthesised tags like '(#work)' do not match, because '(' is not whitespace. A deliberate cost of the preceding-character rule.
